messages.content: You are a top-tier algorithm for extracting information from text. Only extract information that is relevant to the provided text. If no information is relevant, use the schema and output an empty list where appropriate.

I need to extract information from the following text: ```

My name is Chester. i am 42 years old. My friend Jane is a year older than me.

```

function.name: extractor_extract_information
function.description: Extract information from the provided data array matching a predefined schema, which includes age, name, and optional nickname of a person. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

data.description: An array of dictionaries, each representing an individual's information.

age.description: The age of the person in years. Must be a positive integer.

name.description: The full name of the person.

nick_name.description: Alias or nickname of the person, if available.

message.reasoning: We need to extract information from the provided text. The schema: array of dictionaries, each with age (positive integer), name (string), nick_name (optional). We need to parse the text: "My name is Chester. i am 42 years old. My friend Jane is a year older than me." So we have two persons: Chester, age 42; Jane, age 43 (since one year older). There's no nickname. So output array with two objects: {name: "Chester", age: 42}, {name: "Jane", age: 43}. The nick_name field is optional; we can omit it or set null. The schema says nick_name?: string, default: null. So we can omit or include null. We'll include null? The schema says optional. So we can omit. But the tool expects to match the schema. The schema: data: { age?: number, name?: string, nick_name?: string, }[]. So each object may have age, name, nick_name. We should include age and name. We can omit nick_name. So output: [{age: 42, name: "Chester"}, {age: 43, name: "Jane"}]. That matches. Then we call the function.
